Today (the 17th), netizens posted clips on social media showing a suspected CCTV footage taken in a back alley, depicting three people chatting on site. At least two of them were clearly shown wearing the uniform of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD). Based on the FEHD's uniform information, the two are suspected to be a Hawker Management Officer and a Senior Hawker Management Officer.

The footage shows two officer-grade personnel chatting in a back alley. One of them first took out a cigarette and started smoking. Another Senior Hawker Management Officer then walked over, took out a cigarette pack and a lighter, flicked his hair casually, put a cigarette into his mouth, and when he walked away with his back to the camera, a wisp of smoke was seen drifting around him.

The Collective Report inquired with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department whether the people in the footage were FEHD staff. The department confirmed in response to the inquiry that the people in the footage were members of the FEHD's District Hawker Management Team. The spokesperson said the incident occurred in early June this year. When the reporter asked whether FEHD personnel are allowed to smoke while wearing uniform, whether the personnel had violated regulations if the footage were genuine, and whether this would affect the department's image, the FEHD replied that according to established departmental regulations, personnel are prohibited from smoking while wearing uniform and in public places.

The FEHD stated that the department attaches great importance to the discipline and professional conduct of its staff, and has initiated a disciplinary investigation into the incident, and will handle it appropriately according to established procedures and the investigation results. The spokesperson also pointed out that the department has clear requirements on the conduct of personnel while wearing uniform, and any behavior violating departmental disciplinary requirements will be followed up seriously.
